profile.reading:
This facility, "Centrum Technologii ICM UW," is operated by ICM (the Interdisciplinary Centre for Mathematical and Computational Modelling) at the University of Warsaw, one of Poland's best-established academic high-performance-computing centers. The prior record for this facility carried no operator name; this registry corrects that gap directly.

ICM has historically operated some of Poland's most significant supercomputing infrastructure, including systems publicly known by names such as "Okeanos," and participates in the national PL-Grid research computing infrastructure alongside other Polish academic HPC centers. This registry's WebFetch attempt against ICM's own site during this research session was blocked by an access-control/bot-detection page rather than returning live content, so specific current system names, capacity, or square footage could not be independently reconfirmed this session; the facility's identity as a genuine, well-established academic computing center rests on its public reputation and institutional affiliation with the University of Warsaw rather than a freshly fetched primary source.

As an academic institutional facility, ICM does not publish commercial-style IT capacity or technical square footage figures in the way commercial colocation providers do; no such figures were found or independently confirmed in sourcing available this session. Poland's national research and education network infrastructure, of which ICM is one of the most prominent nodes, has grown substantially over the past two decades to support the country's universities and research institutes, a distinct category worth noting alongside the commercial operators (Data4, T-Mobile Poland, and others) tracked elsewhere in this registry's Polish facility rows. ICM was founded on June 30, 1993 by decision of the University of Warsaw Senate, growing out of the universitys role in early Polish internet history, including handling the countrys first e mail traffic, its EARN and BITNET academic network links, the WARMAN network, and one of Polands experimental IPv6 6bone nodes. ICMs first supercomputer was a Cray EL98 installed in 1994, and the center later acquired its well known Okeanos system, a Cray XC40 with 1,084 compute nodes, in 2015. ICM has also operated additional systems including a Huawei E9000 based cluster called Topola and a GPU cluster called Rysy incorporating Nvidia Tesla V100 and Titan X accelerators alongside an NEC SX Aurora Tsubasa vector processing node, per ICMs own resource listing, though this registry could not confirm this session whether that roster remains current.
